# Multi-Level Implementation Task Table (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document expands the phase sequence of
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) into
> **three levels of tasks that can be committed and verified independently**.
>
> The RFC-039 body is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates; this document only
> breaks the work down to an executable granularity and records conflicts that have not yet been
> adjudicated.

## Scope and Positioning

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the RFC-039 phase sequence                             |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each able to be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                      |

**Reserved numbering (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also reserved (2026-11-25). None of the three has
ever had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and the
repository contains no references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test
revival and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8 numbering
aligns with phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding of
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered here**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale for phase
order (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered Level 2/Level 3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which it truly belongs, which may differ
from its containing section) and “**Blocks the mainline**”. `Pending scheduling` is no longer the
default status; an unmarked entry is considered **not schedulable**. Numbering must be **unique
across the entire document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable), written on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write the fix,
the criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**: those
belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board, not a process diary.
**Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “user ruling Jia/Yi/Bing,” “Jia
proposal,” “Proposal A,” “the final implementation is…” and similar text must not appear in this
table. The board answers only “is it complete?”; consult commit messages and the RFC-039 decision
register for rulings and results.

**Short hashes are determined after pushing**: a closure row records the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the closure row**
(see “Commit hashes are obtained after push” in [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The
closure commit itself carries no hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains only numbers**: the Level 1/2/3 counts under `Scope and Positioning`
contain only current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” of eight documents into this table, **five hard gaps
in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Resolution                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps**. RFC defines P5 (checker splitting) and acceptance (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents has a section describing how to perform the split; a single `annotations.rs` line appeared in the directory tree of `01-routing.md`, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                                             | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                         |
| G2  | **The three ownership slots for the `include!` refactor have no implementation**. RFC lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` S7 also lists it. However, the modification list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                          | The implementation steps belong in §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC and 06 now point here                    |
| G3  | **Three competing lists of CI scripts exist**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists another 4 checks (all with different names); `04` also listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts, with no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table         |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life cycle of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines to be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision C1; Pratt is no longer deleted)                                                                       |
| G5  | **Conflicting description of the L2 objective**: RFC and the directory index previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | This has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—no fabrication, no endless filling, and no
patching when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before implementation begins; otherwise, P1 would already be adding `mod` declarations to
`tests/mod.rs` while reviving tests, which is precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Solution)

Source: the defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋ **the
2026-10-07 silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, ruling of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently wrong
> answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, but none of the four requirements may be
> omitted: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely fail); ② do not
> change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled and ran correctly”
> (must not turn them into failures, and must not alter their existing diagnostic codes/text/exit
> codes); ③ register it in the same commit (this row identifies the error type + that phase’s
> revision note + the PR’s required “Error Type” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same
> commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F
> RFC-level design changes still require prior adjudication.** See
> [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria and
> A–F allowlist; **the “default super-refactor followed by registration” approach is not accepted**
> (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, repairs cannot be distinguished from
> regressions, and this conflicts with “no C5′” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: the defect criterion turns green, and **removing the fix must turn it red again**.
**Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow the C2/C3 criteria and the 9.2 gate in P9. **Risk**:
the new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires the corpus differential baseline and
CHANGELOG to be updated in sync.

> **Stop-the-bleed path**: P3 does not need to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus tier) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the correctness defect (`Sorted(3)` silently
> passes) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure work. 3.3 (panic-to-diagnostic) has no
> prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced as a
prerequisite by the ordering constraint**. It is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of
`pub` items” (Rust’s `pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must wholly precede P4**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of all
four refactoring phases; reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and baseline updates
on the new grammar / checker layout / SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `KwPub` and grammar branches                                        | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexer convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                    |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                             |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**; the `pub` branch is moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                              |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (`check_project` body)                                   | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `semantic_tokens`’s `Public` modifier                               | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ir_gen`’s ignored `is_pub` binding                                 | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase directly changes them, but **P6’s hard acceptance requires no differences in `src/std/`** (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-drive tests under `tests/` are exempt as noted in P6’s hard-acceptance section)—they can only land before P6 |

**Additional benefit**: 029g removes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by producers and consumed
nowhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4’s 4.3 obligation ledger
loses one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first land a red criterion before
   code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② under Lib/Script roles,
   unreferenced top-level bindings newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were always exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ corpus
   differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to do first based on available context.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: this section’s incorporation (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) was included in `97071c81b` when the RFC-039 D56 main chain/constraints
> were merged during cleanup of the parallel-flow workspace—the commit message records “3.4
> supplementary registration + D57/D58 rulings documented” and does not mention this track. History
> is not rewritten; it is registered in place according to the existing convention (the `d5b18390`
> precedent, see the P2 landing note), as evidence for later bisecting.

|                                                  | 4.4.4 SMT shared-solver observation ledger `ConsumerStats`/`CONSUMER_STATS`: every production acquisition writes an atomic increment, while production has zero readers (the only reader is `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs`). **Decision ① retain it as decided on 2026-10-24**—write “the only consumer is the test” as a doc contract (preserving the observable-criterion carrier required by D58); decision ② “delete it” is not adopted (that would require simultaneously rewriting 4.4.2’s acceptance criterion, trading off rationale in the 4.4 closure item “sixteen”). **Terminal state**: the three contract sentences are written into the module header of `src/frontend/core/typecheck/proof/smt/backend.rs` and the relevant item documentation comments—① the write surface = one atomic increment per acquisition through the shared interface; ② the read surface contains **only** `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs` (zero production calls); ③ `SolverConsumer::ALL` is a **test-only constant** and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavioral change** (only comments changed; 4.4.2’s acceptance number is unchanged; issue [#475](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/475)) |                                                  | 4.9.9 Cross-unit single-definition method calls lose the formal-parameter name table when using named arguments (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure period): a cross-unit (registry-injected) method called with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` has `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C (primary fix) + Class D inventory (conflicting forms uniformly rejected, pending user ruling)** (old behavior was not successful: for named arguments, the old behavior silently dropped parameters and then failed at runtime or silently produced a wrong value; positional arguments do not consume the name table, but under **name-level ambiguity** (the same type name provided by ≥2 modules) they fall under another criterion: allow when the host module and candidate-provider module have the same source; allow when the modules differ but their candidate signatures agree; for conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers), always reject positional arguments with E1107 (see ④ below)). The mechanism is a **consumer-side key mismatch**—the IR-generation-side formal-name lookup has only three sources: the current unit’s `fn_param_names` / leaf name / module export surface; the first segment of the method key `{Type}.{method}` is a type name rather than a module key and therefore never matches the export surface. **Root cause and fix (single point; no second name table)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::lookup_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`) gains a `method_param_info` source—obtain the formal-name table from the existing unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mixed name ↔ formal-name vectors in the same order; `extract_module_info` ← `method_overload_snapshot`, the same data as the typecheck injection surface), keyed by `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]`, with the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) using the defining unit’s qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` as the lookup key; ② the candidate injection surface’s narrowing rule pairs by target (defining-side type name), while candidates imported through aliases are injected normally; ③ **provider priority** (a bare-name provider with `local == target` takes priority; aliases fill only when no bare name is available; same-level modules with the same full name are skipped) is now a **shared single point**, `frontend::module::import_face::TypeCandidateProviders`—the injection surface (`driver::arms.rs`) and consumer surface (`middle::lower::query`) read the same data and no longer evolve separately; ④ **same-source criterion** (`method_source_mismatch`, `src/middle/lower/query.rs`): let `winner` = the provider module selected by the candidate injection surface and `owner` = the module owning the receiver (the same ownership determination used by `method_dispatch_name`)—`owner == winner` ⇒ allow (typecheck and IR use candidates from the same module; the bare-name positional-argument side is in this case, measured 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0); `owner != winner` ⇒ allow only when the two modules have **exactly identical candidate signatures** for the key (candidate selection does not affect type checking; the value is determined by the receiver’s owning unit—the existing behavior for cross-unit same-named types introduced through inline aliases), otherwise reject loudly (existing E1107). **Positional arguments with identical signatures are still allowed** (4.9.8 fixture 0/0, value determined by the receiver’s unit). Conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers, entire-name injection skipped) use the **conflict branch**: named arguments produce E1014; positional arguments **always produce E1107**—irrespective of argument type, arity, or which side owns the receiver, because the determination depends only on the import surface, so the result is deterministic for the same input. The IR no longer duplicates typecheck’s type-compatibility rules (the previous narrow-compatibility criterion was removed); deterministic support: `all_method_bindings` merges by ascending module key instead of randomly overwriting according to HashMap iteration order. **Delivery (this row is complete)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments obtain the **declaration-time formal-name table** (positive capability, `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ 6.0); ② **name-level ambiguity / conflicting forms deterministically reject loudly** (named arguments E1014, positional arguments E1107, with the determination depending only on the import surface); ③ deterministic repair of `all_method_bindings` by ascending module key (the same input no longer produces different results due to HashMap iteration order). **Completed on 2026-11-26 (fix rounds 1–6 + review rounds 1–6 + closure registration)**; review round 6 independent review passed (criteria and registration completeness). **Class D inventory (each item recorded; based on the direction approved by the user on 2026-11-25—name-level ambiguity is always rejected loudly; inventory here does not imply item-by-item approval)**: 7 examples in conflict/mixed forms that previously worked and now produce E1107—① Int→Float widening (actual literal and variable, pre-t5 0/0 prints 2.5); ② whole-module-import owner (`use c` + `c.Temp(...)`, 0/0 prints 9); ③ mixed-form owner compatibility (0/0 prints 200 / 2.5); ④ same parameters and return type (0/0 prints 200); ⑤ zero-argument same signature `tag()` (0/0 prints 111); ⑥ owner accepts Int + another provider accepts Float + Int actual argument (0/0 prints 200); ⑦ mixed and conflicting forms with same parameters but different return types (0/0 prints 200). **Class C (listed separately; previously unsuccessful and repaired independently as part of this criterion)**: providers with different formal types (pre-t5 already nondeterministic: 0/0 prints 200.0 / E1002 / runtime failure); arity mismatch (pre-t5 0/0 prints 300 = extra actual argument silently dropped, a silent wrong value); named arguments (pre-t5 silently dropped parameters and then produced runtime E6007 → now E1014). **Named arguments** under name-level ambiguity (the same type name provided by ≥2 modules) are still always rejected loudly (the shared criterion’s empty-table exit = existing E1014): the name-table source is untrustworthy and cannot be used to check by name; ⑤ **fallback for “do not silently discard named arguments”**: `reject_named_args_without_param_names` reuses the shared criterion `arg_binding::bind_args_to_params`’s empty-table exit (existing E1014, with `available` using the same empty-string semantics), and is connected to the four IR-side arms that have named arguments but cannot obtain a formal-name table—the RFC-004 binding arm, namespace arm, ordinary method arm without overload resolution, and ordinary **static** function arm; built-in container-constructor arm (`src/middle/lower/expr/container.rs`) likewise rejects named arguments other than `len`; ⑥ **fallback exclusion is determined by binding identity**: closure-value binding (`stmt.rs`’s `closure_fn_names`: the bound value is written as an `=>` lambda and the declaration has no value formal parameters), current-unit top-level function binding (`declared_fn_names`), and **named nested-function declarations** (`nested_functions` entries) are all excluded from the fallback—these three old behaviors all mean “the code compiled and the named arguments were ignored,” and changing the determination to a compile-time error is D59 Class D; all three are registered as known gaps (D60 ② should have been reported but was not, Class A). **Visible changes (list each item; do not merge into “no behavioral change”)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (bare import / alias import / two overload candidates) change from an empty-table E1014 to binding by name (measured 6.0 / 30); ② alias-import (single provider) method named arguments change from silently dropping parameters (runtime `E6007`) to binding by name (6.0); ③ g9g generic curried-method named arguments change from silently dropping parameters (`b.v` reads Void, runtime `E6007 Void vs Int`) to compile-time E1014 (Class C); ④ cross-unit ordinary-function named arguments change from silently dropping parameters to E1014 (Class C); ⑤ const-generic receiver-method named arguments change from silently dropping parameters to E1014 (Class C; the same form with **positional** arguments still fails due to an existing independent defect, outside this task); ⑥ built-in container construction `Vec(Int)(foo = 3)` changes from silent ignoring to E1014 (Class C; `Vec(Int)(len = 3)` remains 0/0 and has the value assertion `v.length == 3`); ⑦ whole-module import (`use lib` + `lib.Circle(...)`) named arguments change from silently dropping parameters to E1014 (Class C); ⑧ **named arguments on name-level ambiguous types** always produce E1014; positional arguments: `owner == winner` and `owner != winner` with identical candidate signatures are allowed (value assertions 4.0 / 200 / 20); different sources with inconsistent signatures, or conflicting forms, always produce E1107 (the three measured silent-wrong-value examples have been eliminated: different formal types, different arity, and different return type; the conflict-form cost inventory is in this row’s Class D inventory); ⑨ named arguments on closure-value bindings (top-level `f = () => 7` and function-body forms), block-body function declarations (`f: (a: Int) -> Int = { 7 }`), and named nested-function declarations (body ignores formal parameters) **retain the old behavior** (named arguments are ignored, measured result 7), and the determination is unchanged. **Residual / known gaps**: named arguments on the above three declaration surfaces are still silently ignored (Class A, D60 ② should have been reported but was not); the formal-name table for named nested functions has not yet been connected to `lookup_param_info`; `E1014` text limitation: an empty `available` means “IR did not obtain a name table,” not “the function truly has no such parameter,” and this task does not change the text or expand the diagnostic surface; the same-source criterion’s signature comparison is structural equivalence (it does not compare implementations), and the residual risk of “identical signature, different implementation” is described in 4.9.10. **Criteria**: 30 driver-level direct-drive cases in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (cross-unit named arguments / alias import / two overload candidates selecting by name / table-driven multiple columns / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding / mixed-import named arguments E1014 + bare-name positional arguments 0/0 (4.0) + alias-side formal-type/arity/return-type three cases E1107 + alias-side same-name formal parameter E1014 / two bare-name-provider conflicts E5006 / top-level closure old behavior Int(7) / function-body closure old behavior / named nested function ignoring formal parameters old behavior Int(7) / container-constructor rejection + `len` value assertion / two alias conflicts (named arguments E1014, positional arguments always E1107) + seven conflict-boundary examples (Int→Float widening literal/variable, whole-module-import owner, mixed owner compatibility, arity mismatch, zero-argument tag(), owner Int + Float provider + Int actual argument) / **invariant criteria**: named arguments under ambiguity must be red + positional arguments with identical signatures are 0/0 and dispatch to the receiver’s owning module (200 / 20)), module guard `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (empty name table ⇒ `None`; deleting the guard turns it red), and project-level fixtures `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method{,-alias-overload}`. **Completion revision**: first fix `02ed42d2`, fallback and `method_param_info` hardening `091b835b`, mixed-import provider priority and container rejection `5edfb53e`, review round (name-level ambiguity rejection / closure-value identity / top-level closure / value assertion) `7e96a844`, this round’s same-source criterion and shared provider table `c861088e`, fix round 5 (conflict visibility / deterministic merge) `a056d30c`, fix round 6 (positional arguments in conflicting forms always E1107) `9498ca98`, fix round 7 (completion of Class D inventory and C/D classification, criteria +2) `8ec25cb1`, and this row’s closure registration (review round 6 pass: criteria and registration completeness) = the commit to which this row belongs. **Regression surface**: zero IR snapshot drift, corpus parity 405 cases (403 existing cases byte-for-byte unchanged + 2 new fixtures), and the six dispatch criteria of 4.9.8 remain green; the five unit tests in `src/frontend/module/import_face.rs` cover conflict alias / bare+alias two-level conflicts for providers/winner/provider_count/injected_pairs. | 4.9.7         | Criteria are in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and this row’s “Criteria”; |                                                  | 4.9.10 Undefined cross-unit method identity (registered 2026-11-25, structural issue confirmed during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` contains no module qualification, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`arms.rs::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—**each guess the provider independently**, and changing any one moves the “silent wrong value” elsewhere. 4.9.9’s stop-the-bleed criterion is: under name-level ambiguity, named arguments always produce E1014; positional arguments—same source (candidate-provider module == receiver-owning module) are allowed, different sources with identical candidate signatures are allowed, and **conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers) always produce E1107** (the IR does not duplicate typecheck’s compatibility rules); the root-cause solution = upgrade the method key to a **module-qualified identity**, produce it from one resolver, and have all three consumers read it; this requires changing the shape of `overload_resolutions` keys and mixed names (D59 **Class D**, requires adjudication) ### P5 In-File Checker Split — Supplemented by This Document (Original Gap G1)

Source: RFC definition + `01-routing.md` directory tree + hard constraint (the `pub(crate)` path of
`collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.1 `include!` → real `mod`** (2 Level 3 tasks)
- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 Level 3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 Level 3 tasks)

| Level 2                     | Level 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Prerequisite | Acceptance                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → real `mod` | 5.1.1 Change the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` to a real `mod` declaration (do not hard-code line anchors; measured at the final line of the file at the time)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | P4 complete  | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                                        |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or explicit imports (`include!` implicitly inherited the scope in its day)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                          |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move the refinement blocks (three non-contiguous ranges in the original `checker.rs`; now a single `checker/refinement.rs` containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), while leaving the retained surface and six cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                    |
|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point as “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving `impl`**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer implicitly writes to the error channel through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned upward, and the sole write point is the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol located). **Rationale for remaining in `impl`**: the only field used by this family is `self.env` (technically, leaving `impl` is feasible), but converting the entry point and entire walk to free functions would move all call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 producers (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 producers + 1 test, and it would create a reverse dependency from the retained surface (signature collection) to refinement—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to remove | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                               |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move the 10-member annotation-validation family (now a single `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                    |
|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and measurement in 5.3.1 confirmed that it was **not migrated** ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already met**, so **do not add** a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is migrated with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | 5.3.1        | **Zero caller changes** is the hard acceptance criterion for this step: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is later migrated with the annotation family, **then** `checker.rs` must add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; measurement in 5.3
confirmed that it was **not migrated**, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was
already met).

**Only split confirmed large blocks. **Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—that increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split after they grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> the same compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument
> view and implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a
> **pure decision** (normalize both sides and compare; do not bind type variables); evidence is the
> **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (closed terms and open
> terms/recursion both hold); Σ constructor sites **reuse** the same evidence interface rather than
> establishing another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not merely that subphase
> names have completed.**

> **6.9 closure criterion**: I1–I5 and I7 all hold, I6 is closed according to the design-review
> conclusion for 6.9.5 (does not block P7), and every I8 slice has evidence; residual items
> #537/#539/#540/#541/#542/#552 all have a disposition (fixed/explicitly excluded/separate task);
> #542 landed on 2026-11-19. **Do not use “all subphases checked” as a substitute for the invariants
> holding.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 ruling → A.C3; decision-point protocol
> → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require file-surface
> coordination (C3 leans toward typecheck→mono, d toward types/solver→sema), and C.2 may run in
> parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (does not depend on defeq). D’s implementation waits for
> confirmation of the B design package and depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and may
> depend on the 6.9.3 typed exit. **The P7 gate = exits A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 ruling (A ruled on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording “`CheckOnly`
> evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been deleted; the
> current mechanism is that an open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is created, and
> the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`. **The ruling was
> changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a representation (Jia: open
> terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / Yi: do not specialize); D-b
> evaluation point (mono only; Bing-1’s second field and Bing-2 reconstruction from IR both break
> the single representation/evaluator, Bing-3 = Jia); **F4-T termination** (naive firing drives the
> recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a instantiate a conditional inside the term /
> T-b bounded firing + return the original at the boundary / T-c a termination layer or revise the
> specification). **Implement first, then rule; before measurement, “Jia is implementable” must not
> be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=Jia-closed, D-b=Bing-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8;
> C3 implementation is a separate task; do not claim complete I4.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 states that “a
> decision point first uses unification; after unification fails, definitional equality may be used,
> but all partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables);
> what are the snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; do unify and defeq share one budget or have
> separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtyping/Any/Never;
> defeq only decides equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional subtyping must not
> be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call graph before
> writing code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract has already wasted two rounds by assuming `can_assign`
> was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or an itemized classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ idempotence of the error-code generator (if emission points/code tables
> change); ④ red before green for behavioral changes classified under D59. **Wiring tasks
> additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many
> paths, which paths are reachable); using unit-test reachability as a substitute for user
> reachability is prohibited; rollback and budget require measured values. **Residual handling**:
> #537 (Class D, silent discard of proof-function formal-parameter refinement; do not fix before
> adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; Class C stage
> boundary; if it remains open, 6.9.4 covers only module-local cases), #540 (deep-nesting stack
> overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack orchestration thread +
> parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three sites entered/left together: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the single
> `rewritten_call_target` point, and init sections and function bodies share one site-rewriting
> implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed
> (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + two post-mono entry points connected + C2c temporary workaround
> removed; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552 (imported
> multi-parameter predicate proof execution; adjacent to 6.9.5, separate task). **Ownership pending
> adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency`
> do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge; a ruling is needed on whether they remain in
> 6.9.4 outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim that Π/Σ is complete; 6.9.4 only covers constant equalities and does
> not implement the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is
> outside this item; witness erasure ≠ runtime-check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5
> cover only forms that do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if #539 is not
> fixed, 6.9.4 covers only module-local cases; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 landed (2026-11-19);
> 2.1.4’s inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (criterion rewritten around slot
> identity) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a gate are met.

**Hard acceptance** (**2026-10-27 revision, following the 2026-10-26 ruling ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required, but each
modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be relaxed**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new diagnostic
code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is handled as a
separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original wording of 2026-10-26 ruling ② was
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-diff requirement to all of `tests/`;
> the revised wording **only changes direct-drive test files from “zero diff” to “may be modified
> but file / line count / reason must be registered”**, while the **zero-diff requirements for the
> corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library
> (`src/std/`) remain unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs`

> **There is no line-count ratchet script** (`check-file-size.py` + `baseline.toml` were cancelled
> on 2026-10-03). Scale problems are addressed through `08` Prohibition 2 criterion A (separation of
> responsibilities, manual judgment).

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleed path (ruling of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to **2.3.2 +
> 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus tier + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2
> snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed in parallel with
> P3. Stopping correctness defects must not be blocked by criterion-infrastructure work; however,
> **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all three criterion tiers to be
> in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must **be written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus tier (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order lets the stage table fossilize bugs as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface covers P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 rewrite targets (the list appears in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, checker layout, and IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations are not converged first, the new IR grows into a third representation; **the P7 gate = exits A/B/C of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; that is, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface and must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                  | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                      |
| B                                      | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod` and can be reverted by file                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| C                                      | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion tiers are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D                                      | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                       |
| E                                      | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| F                                      | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be captured last                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| G                                      | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 changes `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 changes `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 changes two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub`-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite batch for P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only the
  D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original gap G3’s three competing lists
  made closure impossible. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each owned by one phase
  (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hard-conversion timing
  explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar,
  checker layout, and IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplemented by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the
  largest single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says that “fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record “what was fixed.” **Execution
  convention**: each 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two exclusive
  commits per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames, and a missed change **silently changes
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, and the deletion
  remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally planned as “separate issues”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as future work.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.
